title: Construction of pinned cone filtration steps
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be a Grothendieck abelian category [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian], $K$ an integer-indexed cochain complex, $I$ a bicomplex with complex index $s\in\mathbf Z$ and resolution index $r\in\mathbf N$ [def-sp-double-complex-total], and $a:K[0]\to I$ a bicomplex map, where $K[0]$ concentrates each $K^s$ in resolution degree zero. Let $b\in\mathbf Z$ and suppose $I^{s,\bullet}=0$ and $K^s=0$ for $s<b$. Let $J$ be the identity-mapped, extended-by-zero and flipped bicomplex [def-sp-cartan-eilenberg-presentation], and let $\epsilon:K\to\operatorname{Tot}(J)$ be a chain map whose component in degree $n$ is $a^{n,0}$ followed by the extension identification and the $(0,n)$ diagonal inclusion. Set $C=\operatorname{Cone}(\epsilon)$, using the mapping cone of [lem-pur-quasi-iso-cone-acyclic], with canonical inclusions $u_n:K^{n+1}\to C^n$ and $v_n:\operatorname{Tot}(J)^n\to C^n$. There is a decreasing subcomplex filtration $F$ of $C$ [def-sp-filtration] with degreewise steps [def-sp-filtered-complex-subquotients] $F^pC^n=(\operatorname{im}(u_n)\text{ if }p\le n+1\text{, else }0)+\sum_{s=\max(b,p)}^n\operatorname{im}(J^{n-s,s}\to\operatorname{Tot}(J)^n\xrightarrow{v_n}C^n)$. The sum is the finite supremum of image subobjects, with empty sum zero.

source.place: Homology, Tag 0133, lemma-double-complex-gives-resolution, canonical augmentation and finite-diagonal filtration; augmented-cone form of the argument, with Tag 012W

proof.text: Construct the degreewise steps from the formula in the statement, using the actual cone summand inclusions and diagonal coprojections. The finite supremum records precisely the resolution summands with complex index at least p; the remaining summands outside [b,n] vanish. Interval containment and monotonicity of the optional K summand make these subobjects antitone.

proof.text: The cone differential is minus d_K on its K summands, the total differential on its I summands, and epsilon in its off-diagonal block. Each preserves or raises complex index. The equation specifying epsilon identifies the off-diagonal block with the complex-index-(n+1) summand, so this block also preserves the filtration. Factor through the monic step arrows; uniqueness gives square-zero lifts and antitone inclusions of the resulting subcomplexes.
